user.title: HA Irrigation Controller
user.description: Pick the pump and sensors this controller drives, then set the cycle start times. Zones are added afterwards.

data_description.pump_switch: The switch that powers the pump feeding your valves.
data_description.rain_sensor: A sensor reporting accumulated precipitation in millimetres. Required: watering is modulated by rainfall.
data_description.temperature_sensor: Optional. Stored for future weather coefficients; it is not used in this version.
data_description.humidity_sensor: Optional. Stored for future weather coefficients; it is not used in this version.
data_description.morning_enabled: Off by default: in spring the evening cycle alone is usually enough. The evening cycle always runs.
data_description.morning_start: Local time the morning cycle starts, when it is enabled.
data_description.evening_start: Local time the evening cycle starts.
data_description.actuation_timeout: Seconds to wait for a pump or valve switch to confirm a command before raising an anomaly. The cycle continues either way.
data_description.manual_timeout: Minutes a valve or the pump may stay open after you switch it on by hand before the controller closes it itself and tells you. 1 to 240 minutes, 30 by default. It cannot be turned off. Changing it reloads the integration, which ends any pause in progress and drops the timeout of a switch already open by hand — nothing then closes that switch until you switch it off and on again.
data_description.notify_target: Optional. A notify entity (for example your phone's companion app) that receives one push notification when an anomaly opens. Leave empty for no push notifications; anomalies still appear under Settings → Repairs.

error.start_times_conflict: The morning and evening cycles cannot start at the same time. Change one of them, or turn the morning cycle off.
error.pump_is_own_entity: This is the irrigation controller's own Season switch, not a physical pump. Pick the switch that powers your pump.
error.notify_target_is_own_entity: This is one of the irrigation controller's own entities, not a notify target. Pick the notify entity of a phone or messaging service.

user.title: Add zone
user.description: Model one physical irrigation zone: the valve that feeds it, how long it waters per cycle, and how rain affects it.

data_description.name: How this zone appears everywhere: its device, the dashboard card, notifications.
data_description.valve_switch: The switch that opens this zone's valve. Each zone needs its own valve — not the pump switch.
data_description.morning_duration: Minutes this zone waters during the morning cycle.
data_description.evening_duration: Minutes this zone waters during the evening cycle.
data_description.rain_exposed: On for zones that receive rainfall. Sheltered zones (greenhouse, covered beds) are never rain-reduced.
data_description.rain_factor: Minutes of watering credited per millimetre of rain, applied only to rain-exposed zones. 0 disables the reduction. The default of 1 min/mm is deliberately conservative — tune it across the season.

cancel_cycle.name: Cancel cycle
cancel_cycle.description: Stops the cycle that is running right now. The open valve is closed, then the pump, and the cycle is recorded as cancelled. This is the only thing that stops a running cycle.

run_now.name: Run now
run_now.description: Starts a full cycle immediately, exactly as a scheduled one: the pump first, then every zone in order on its configured duration for the cycle you name. It runs even when the season is off, and it is refused while another cycle is already running or waiting to start.

cycle.name: Cycle
cycle.description: Which of the two daily cycles to run. Each zone stores a separate duration for each, so this is what decides how long every zone waters.

set_season.name: Set season
set_season.description: Turns watering on or off in one action. With the season off no new cycle is scheduled and no anomaly is raised; a cycle already running still finishes.

enabled.name: Enabled
enabled.description: On resumes scheduling from this moment on. Off suspends it, including any cycle already queued behind a running one.

set_zone_duration.name: Set zone duration
set_zone_duration.description: Changes how long one zone waters during one cycle. The change applies without restarting Home Assistant. A cycle running at that moment finishes with its original durations; the new value is applied when the running cycle completes.

zone_id.name: Zone
zone_id.description: The zone's identifier. This is the config subentry id shown in the error message if you get it wrong — not the zone's name.

cycle.name: Cycle
cycle.description: Which of the two daily cycles this duration applies to.

duration.name: Duration
duration.description: Minutes this zone waters during that cycle, from 1 to 120. The two cycles must not end up overlapping.

pump_on_unconfirmed.title: Pump did not confirm turning on

confirm.title: Pump did not confirm turning on
confirm.description: The pump switch `{entity_id}` did not report ON within the actuation timeout during cycle `{cycle_id}`. The cycle continued anyway (fail-wet): the zones ran their slots, possibly without pressure. Check the switch and the pump. Acknowledging clears this issue; it also clears itself when the pump next confirms turning on.

pump_off_unconfirmed.title: Pump did not confirm turning off

confirm.title: Pump did not confirm turning off
confirm.description: The pump switch `{entity_id}` did not report OFF within the actuation timeout. The pump may still be running against closed valves — check it now. Cycle: `{cycle_id}` (`-` when the pump was not being switched off for a cycle, for example after it was left on by hand or at startup recovery). Acknowledging clears this issue; it also clears itself when the pump next confirms turning off.

confirm.title: Valve did not confirm opening
confirm.description: The valve `{entity_id}` of zone `{zone_id}` did not report ON within the actuation timeout during cycle `{cycle_id}`. The zone's slot elapsed anyway and the missed watering is carried forward as water debt. Check the valve and its switch. Acknowledging clears this issue; it also clears itself when the valve next confirms opening.

confirm.title: Valve did not confirm closing
confirm.description: The valve `{entity_id}` (zone `{zone_id}`) did not report OFF within the actuation timeout. The valve may still be open — check it now. Nothing was stopped on account of it: a cycle that was running continued with its next zone, and a valve closed because it had been left open by hand is not commanded again. Cycle: `{cycle_id}` (`-` when the close did not belong to a cycle). Acknowledging clears this issue; it also clears itself when the valve next confirms closing.

journal_save_failed.title: Cycle journal could not be saved

confirm.title: Cycle journal could not be saved
confirm.description: Home Assistant's storage refused a write of the irrigation journal. Watering continued; a restart during this window could lose the last transitions. Check the free space and the permissions of the `.storage` folder. Acknowledging clears this issue; it also clears itself when the next journal write succeeds.

confirm.title: Configured entity is missing
confirm.description: The entity `{entity_id}` (role: `{role}`, zone: `{zone_id}`) was removed from or disabled in the entity registry. Nothing is skipped: the next cycle still commands it and will report unconfirmed actuations. Restore or re-enable the entity, or reconfigure the controller or the zone. Acknowledging clears this issue; it also clears itself when the entity comes back enabled, or when the role is reconfigured to another entity or the zone deleted.

confirm.title: A cycle was interrupted
confirm.description: Cycle `{cycle_id}` was interrupted while it was running (zone `{zone_id}`) because the integration was reloaded, disabled or removed. The open valve and the pump were closed. When the integration loads again the cycle is recovered: resumed on the same irrigation day, otherwise closed with the missed watering carried forward as water debt. Acknowledging clears this issue; it also clears itself when the cycle is recovered, or when the next cycle completes or is cancelled.

cycle_recovered.title: A cycle was recovered at startup

confirm.title: A cycle was recovered at startup
confirm.description: Cycle `{cycle_id}` was found in progress in the journal when the integration loaded (zone `{zone_id}` is the zone that was watering, `-` when none was). Any valve or pump of that cycle still on was switched off first. Outcome: `{outcome}` — `resumed` means the cycle continued on the same irrigation day with its original durations; `closed` means it was on an earlier day and was filed as interrupted, with each zone's missed watering carried forward as water debt; `discarded` means the journaled cycle could not be read, so every configured valve and the pump were switched off and nothing was booked. Acknowledging clears this issue; it does not clear itself.

missed_cycle.title: A scheduled cycle did not run

confirm.title: A scheduled cycle did not run
confirm.description: The `{kind}` cycle was scheduled but its watering window closed with no record of it: cycle `{cycle_id}` is filed as missed. Home Assistant was most likely down over the window, or the start fell inside the hour the clocks skip forward. Outcome: `{outcome}` — `rerun` means the cycle is watering right now, on the same irrigation day and on freshly calculated durations, and this happens at most once per missed cycle; `recorded` means the day's later cycle had already run, so nothing is watered on top of it and each zone's missed watering is carried forward as water debt, capped at one base duration. Acknowledging clears this issue; it does not clear itself.

manual_valve_timeout.title: A switch left open by hand was closed

confirm.title: A switch left open by hand was closed
confirm.description: The switch `{entity_id}` was switched on by hand and stayed open longer than the safety timeout, so the controller switched it off. Nothing else was changed, and no watering was cut short. Any cycle held back while you were on site starts as soon as the last hand-opened switch is off — including by this timeout. To keep a switch open for longer, switch it off and on again on site: the timeout starts over from that moment. Acknowledging clears this issue; it does not clear itself.
